headline: Six of seven majors above their 200-day line, but the daily candle is red across most of them
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it's the cleanest read on the board: BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, BNB and DOGE all sit above their 200-day moving averages with golden crosses confirmed on the first three plus BNB. Only ADA sits below its 200-day, a full 76.3% off its 12-month high of $0.9304. That's a market where the trend structure is broadly intact even though bitcoin itself is still 37.2% under its own 12-month peak of $124,739.81. One asset below trend and six above is not a fragile tape, but note that every major is also down on the day, from BTC's -0.89% to DOGE's -1.06%, while the 7-day and 30-day windows are mostly green. That's the kind of window disagreement worth naming out loud rather than smoothing over: BTC is down 0.9% today, up 0.2% on the week, up 23.1% on the month. Same asset, three different stories depending on the lens.

Momentum is where it gets more interesting. RSI-14 readings cluster in the high 50s to high 60s (BNB tops the group at 68.5) which is firm but not stretched. Yet MACD has crossed below signal on BTC, ETH, SOL and XRP, the four largest names by this list, while it sits above signal on BNB, DOGE and ADA. That's a genuine divergence: price structure says uptrend, RSI says room left, but the MACD read on the majors says short-term momentum has already rolled over and is resting, not accelerating. Worth watching whether that cools further or resolves back upward.

Positioning tells a mixed story depending on where you look. BTC funding on OKX is a modest 0.0029% per 8 hours (3.2% annualized), unremarkable, and open interest is a hefty $2.17B, so there's real size in the boat without an expensive toll to sit in it. ETH funding is similarly tame at 4.0% annualized against $1.5B open interest. Compare that to XRP and DOGE, where funding runs 10.2% and 11.0% annualized respectively, longs badly outnumber shorts (long/short ratios of 2.27 and 3.34), and liquidations in XRP's case skew hard toward longs getting flushed ($238K in long liquidations look small against $1.09M in short liquidations, meaning shorts have actually taken the bigger hit recently). SOL stands apart with negative funding (-4.4% annualized), meaning shorts are paying longs to hold their position there, an unusual tell in a market otherwise leaning bullish on positioning.

Flows add a layer of confirmation on the institutional side. BTC spot ETFs posted a net inflow of $174.6M on 04 Sep 2026, and the last five sessions net to $986.7M inflow with three straight days in the same direction. ETH ETFs took in $25.9M on the same date, $215.3M over five sessions. That's real traditional-finance demand showing up while the daily candles are red, a genuine tension. Whale flows over the trailing week (ending Sep 08) show $28M net moving off exchanges, a reversal from the prior three weeks which each saw large net inflows onto exchanges (Aug 18: $438M onto, Aug 25: $1,094M onto, Sep 01: $49M onto). BTC specifically saw $134.1M move off exchanges this week while ETH saw $106.1M move onto exchanges, opposite directions for the two largest assets. Stablecoin float is up 1.35% over 30 days to $310.1B, dry powder building modestly rather than draining.

Sentiment sits at 69, labeled Greed, within a 30-day range of 27 to 74, so it's near the top of its recent band while nearly every major asset closed the day lower. The crowd feels good, the tape printed red, and the ETF desks kept buying anyway. That gap between a greedy gauge and a red day is itself the story. What to watch from here: whether BTC and ETH's MACD crosses back above signal (momentum resuming) or open interest and funding on XRP/DOGE unwind from their crowded long tilt, and whether the whale flow flips back onto exchanges next week or the current off-exchange week holds.
